Subject: Order Form - Term & Renewal Questions

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the draft order form. Procurement has two principal asks we need to resolve before we can move to legal redlines:

- Auto-renew: Helix prefers either no auto-renew (manual renewal only) or a mutual opt-in auto-renew with a 90-120 day notice window.
- Termination for convenience: we need language that allows Helix to terminate for convenience with at least 90 days' notice and a pro-rated refund for pre-paid committed spend.

Can Redwood confirm whether these are acceptable or propose a compromise? Also attaching our internal procurement guidance (see OrderForm_HLX_2025.pdf).

We would like to set up a legal-to-legal call if Redwood will be pushing back on either item.

Thanks,
Sarah

Head of Procurement

Subject: Re: Order Form - Term & Renewal Questions

Sarah — thanks for the clear callouts and for the Order Form attachment. Quick replies below and then a proposed path forward: 

- Auto-renew: Redwood's standard is 12-month term with automatic renewal unless notice is given. We can be flexible on notice windows for enterprise customers.
- Termination for convenience: we normally allow mutual termination with pro-rated refunds for unused prepaid credits, but we also have non-cancellable commitments tied to reserved capacity.

Proposed path forward (so we can get to legal redlines quickly):
1) I'll loop Legal and Sales (cc'd) to prepare a tracked MSA/Order Form that implements these options as *negotiable tiers*:
   - Pilot / evaluation: no auto-renew (opt-out) or 30-day manual termination.
   - Production (>= $250k ARR): mutual 90-day notice for termination for convenience with pro-rated refund and transition assistance.
   - Reserved capacity (dedicated): additional buyout language if customer wants to exit early (to cover un-amortized infra costs).
2) If Helix needs 120-day notice due to internal change controls, call that out and we will evaluate on a case-by-case basis.

I'll attach a tracked MSA from Legal tomorrow. Would you be available for a 30-minute legal-to-legal call Thurs or Fri?

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
VP, Sales Engineering

Subject: Re: Order Form - Term & Renewal Questions (MSA redline attached)

Hi all — I reviewed Helix's ask. High-level Legal position and proposed redlines attached (Redwood_MSA_v3_track_changes.docx):

- Auto-renew: We prefer to keep auto-renew for standard SaaS orders to avoid service gaps. Compromise: allow customer to opt-out by giving notice within a 60-90 day window prior to renewal for production contracts; for pilots, we can remove auto-renew entirely.
- Notice windows: 60 days mutual notice will be our baseline. We can accept 90 days for enterprise production deals > $250k with legal pre-approval.
- Termination for convenience: Redwood will accept mutual termination for convenience with pro-rated refunds for prepaid amounts, subject to: (i) a defined transition assistance period (30-90 days depending on service), and (ii) buyout for non-cancellable reserved capacity that reflects remaining committed payments.

Action items for Helix legal to consider: confirm whether your requirement is (A) 90 days notice for any termination, or (B) 90 days only for production-level agreements. Also confirm whether you require a full refund for prepaid committed spend or a pro-rated credit.

I attached the tracked MSA with comment balloons on Sections 2 (Term), 3 (Renewal), and 11 (Termination for Convenience). Happy to join a legal call.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Laura — thanks for the detailed read. A few clarifications from Helix: 

- The 90-day requirement is driven by internal governance and regulator notification processes for provider change; it applies to all customer-facing production agreements. For pilot/eval projects we can accept shorter windows, but we often want a 120-day opt-out period for pilots that touch PHI or integrations.
- On refunds: Helix requires a pro-rated refund of prepaid committed spend; buyouts for reserved capacity are acceptable but need a clear amortization schedule.

We are available for legal-to-legal Thursday 10–11am PT or Friday 9–10am PT. Please confirm and send a calendar invite with dial-in.

Thanks,
Sarah

Subject: Next steps — proposed compromise & action items

Folks — summarizing the proposed compromise so we can get to a redline and call: 

1) Term & Auto-renew
   - Pilot/eval: remove auto-renew; allow 120-day opt-out when integration/PHI is involved.
   - Production: 12-month term + auto-renew by default; Helix may provide 90-day mutual notice to opt-out for production SLAs > $250k (Legal approval required).

2) Termination for convenience
   - Mutual termination with pro-rated refund of prepaid amounts for standard SaaS usage.
   - Reserved/dedicated capacity: termination allowed with a buyout equal to unamortized committed payments (we will propose a 6–12 month amortization schedule to reflect infra spend).

3) Transition assistance & data export
   - Redwood to provide 30–90 days of transition assistance depending on the service and complexity; final duration will be defined in Order Form addendum.

Action items:
- Legal (Laura): Prepare tracked changes implementing the three-tier compromise and add amortization table example for reserved capacity.
- Sales (Ben & Marissa): Confirm threshold ($250k) and whether Helix will be treated as production or pilot for the initial order.
- Helix (Sarah): Confirm preferred call time (you suggested Thurs 10–11am PT or Fri 9–10am PT).

If everyone is aligned, I'll circulate the updated tracked MSA and a short summary term sheet for signature (DocuSign) to unblock procurement.

Thanks all — Karthik
